Icon fixed. TTS explained below.

## Icon

Was ours: filled cone, custom 2.5/5 radius waves. Original (`ncdai/chanhdai.com` → `components/animated-icons/volume-icon.tsx`) is lucide `volume-2` geometry — **stroked** cone, waves `a5 5` + `a9 9` on 24 grid.

Now `components/icons.tsx:98` carries original paths scaled 24→16 grid, stroke-only, house weight 1.25. Rendered size `size-4` → `size-4.5` to match. tsc clean.

## TTS — no model. That is problem.

Our code (`components/pronounce-name.tsx:66`):
```javascript
new SpeechSynthesisUtterance("Droov Sharma") → window.speechSynthesis.speak()
```

Browser Web Speech API. Zero network, zero cost. Voice = whatever OS ships:

- macOS/Safari → Samantha (formant-ish, robotic)
- Chrome desktop → "Google US English" (decent, network)
- Windows → David/Zira (bad)
- Firefox Linux → espeak (very bad)

So sound differs per device, and worst case is awful. Rate forced 0.85 → drags more.

## Original never used TTS

`namePronunciationUrl: "https://assets.chanhdai.com/audio/chanhdai.mp3"` — **recorded human voice**, static file. Played via `useSound` → `fetch` → `decodeAudioData` → `AudioBufferSourceNode` (Web Audio, not `<audio>`, so zero-latency replay).

That is whole gap. No synth can match recording of person saying own name — especially "Dhruv" with breathy-voiced /dʱ/ + retroflex ʋ, which no English voice has phonemes for. Respelling hack ("Droov") only proves it.

## Fix

Slot already exists — `site.pronunciation.audio` takes precedence over synth (`pronounce-name.tsx:57`). Options:

1. **Record self.** Phone voice memo → trim → `public/audio/dhruv.mp3` → set `audio`. Matches original exactly. Best.
2. **Real TTS model**, rendered once to static mp3 (ElevenLabs multilingual, or OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts` with pronunciation instructions). Ships as file, no runtime API. Decent, still not native.
3. Keep browser synth. Bad, as you found.

Want me wire (1) — you drop mp3 in `public/audio/`, I set path + swap playback to Web Audio like original?





\*\*\*

whats your take on the above?

\*\*\*
I’m using the caveman communication skill because you asked for a take, and I’ll keep it blunt and practical. I’m checking the current pronunciation path before I weigh in.

Take: diagnosis right.

Pronunciation = personal identity asset. Browser TTS varies by OS/browser → inconsistent, sometimes bad. Do not ship it as canonical.

Best order:

1. Self-recorded MP3 → highest authenticity, zero runtime cost/vendor risk.
2. One-time generated TTS → acceptable fallback, still less personal.
3. Browser synth → temporary fallback only; ideally remove once recording exists.

Current slot already supports fix:

```text
public/audio/dhruv.mp3
site.pronunciation.audio = "/audio/dhruv.mp3"
```

Keep `new Audio` for now. Web Audio preload/decode only matters if first-tap latency appears. Record clean, trim silence, normalize, export MP3. Then test production replay + mobile Safari.

Yes: use option 1.
but tbh, my voice isnt that great either. what if we use the best tts model to generate the voice, and then use it as an mp3?
I’m checking current TTS options and their official capabilities. “Best” here depends on pronunciation control, voice quality, licensing, and whether you want polished vs personal.

Yes. Better move.

Bad self-recording can hurt more than polished synthetic voice. Static AI MP3 gives consistent sound, zero runtime API, zero device variance.

My pick:

1. **ElevenLabs Multilingual v2** — best default: natural voices, MP3 export, Hindi support, pronunciation dictionaries. [Docs](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/speech-synthesis/p)
2. **Cartesia Sonic 3.5** — best if exact phoneme control matters; supports IPA pronunciation dictionaries. [Docs](https://docs.cartesia.ai/build-with-cartesia/capability-guides/custom-pronunciations)
3. **OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts`** — good if already using OpenAI; supports voice instructions and MP3, but custom voices have eligibility limits. [Docs](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/audio/voice-consent-list)

Do not clone your voice. Clone preserves weak timbre. Use designed/stock voice: warm, calm, neutral, non-theatrical.

Generate 6–10 two-word variants. Blind-test phone + laptop. Pick winner.

```text
Say only: “Dhruv Sharma”.

Warm, calm, concise. Neutral Indian-English delivery.
One natural breath. No introduction. No extra words.
Pronounce “Dhruv” as /dʱruːʋ/, not “droove” or “drove”.
```

Then ship:

```text
public/audio/dhruv.mp3
site.pronunciation.audio = "/audio/dhruv.mp3"
```

This becomes my recommendation over both browser synth and mediocre self-recording.

I’ll check current ElevenLabs voice options, then narrow to voices likely to handle “Dhruv Sharma” without sounding theatrical or American-cartoonish.

Short answer: **don’t pick old stock voices**.

Best route:

- Voice Library → `Professional`
- Language → `Hindi` or `English`
- Accent → `Indian`
- Gender → whatever sounds natural
- Use case → `Narration` / `Conversational`
- `High quality` → on

ElevenLabs says pre-made/generated voices are English; professional community voices carry native-language/accent tags. Search filters support language, accent, gender, use case, quality. [Voice guidance](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/core-capabilities/text-to-speech/which-voices-in-the-voice-library-are-native-to-a-specific-language) · [Voice filters](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/voices/search)

If you want one named starting point: **Darian — Warm Grounded Storyteller**. Backup: **Kellan — Casual Friendly Speaker**. But these are general English voices, not Indian-native. Do blind listening before committing.

Avoid tutorials recommending Rachel, Adam, Antoni, etc. ElevenLabs is replacing old defaults; they expire **December 31, 2026**. [Current voice transition](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/voices/my-voices/what-are-default-voices)

Use model `eleven_multilingual_v2`, not v3 first. v2 = stable, natural, less theatrical. Generate:

```text
Dhruv Sharma.
```

If two-word output sounds stiff, generate:

```text
Hi, I’m Dhruv Sharma.
```

Then trim everything except name. This often sounds more natural. Set stability moderately high, style low. Erotiske
